title: AWS CWI Training in Buffalo, NY: 6-Day Exam Prep
description: Six-day AWS CWI exam prep for Buffalo Niagara welders: stadium and structural steel, bridges, aerospace and plants. Corporate, online or one-to-one.
h1: AWS CWI Exam Prep in Buffalo, New York: Six Days for Niagara Frontier Steel, Bridge and Manufacturing Inspectors
html:
Buffalo has been a steel and manufacturing city for well over a century, and the welding has not stopped: a new stadium in Orchard Park, bridge and highway steel on a border crossing, aerospace parts in East Aurora, copper and metals plants, and a joining research center on the city's East Side. Atlantis NDT prepares Western New York welders, fitters, QC inspectors and engineers for the AWS Certified Welding Inspector (CWI) examination with a six-day (6-day) course built around the exam's three parts: Part A Fundamentals, Part B Practical and Part C Code Application. Candidates choose a corporate course at their employer's facility, online self-paced study with an instructor answering questions, or one-to-one sessions with the instructor, either online or in person. The examination is administered by AWS, which also issues the certification; Atlantis certifies no one. There is no Atlantis classroom in Buffalo, and the company has no office in New York State; its offices are in Houston, Texas and Hyderabad, India. For pricing, send a Buffalo CWI exam prep enquiry.

Three ways to take the six days from Buffalo

All three formats follow the same six-day outline: two days of fundamentals (processes, terminology, joint design, symbols, metallurgy, testing, discontinuities, safety and fabrication math), one day on practical measurement and document work for Part B, one day inside the code book you will use in Part C, one day of timed practice papers and a last day on weak areas and examination logistics. The AWS CWI exam prep course page sets out each day.

  • Corporate. A fabricator, plant or contractor anywhere on the Niagara Frontier books the six days for a group of its own people at its own facility. The practice uses that employer's welds and gauges and, where it fits, its code and procedures.
  • Online. An individual follows a study plan built on the six-day outline, with course materials, original practice questions and timed practice papers, and puts questions to an instructor at any point. There are no class times, which matters for someone on rotating plant shifts or a construction crew working through the short summer season.
  • One-to-one. A single candidate works through six days of one-to-one sessions with the instructor, online or in person at a location agreed when the course is booked.

Atlantis writes all of the practice material itself, against the topic areas AWS publishes. None of it is an AWS examination question, and the course is not approved, accredited or endorsed by AWS.

What the Niagara Frontier welds

The new Highmark Stadium and big structural jobs

The new Highmark Stadium in Orchard Park is the largest structural steel job Western New York has seen in years. The American Institute of Steel Construction reported that it took about 25,000 tons of structural steel, roughly 60 percent of it from New York fabricators. Cives Steel of St. Lawrence County was the prime fabricator, supplying about half, with JPW Structural Contracting of Syracuse, A&T Ironworks of New Rochelle and a dozen other shops also involved. The stadium topped out in 2025. A job like that puts welding inspectors in two places at once: in the fabrication shops, checking fit-up, welder qualification and finished welds before members ship, and in the field, where moment connections and other field welds are made and inspected under the project's inspection plan. AWS D1.1 is the code that governs both.

Bridges, highways and a border crossing

Buffalo sits on the Niagara River with Canada on the other bank, so bridge steel is part of daily life here. State highway bridges in New York are fabricated to AWS D1.5, the Bridge Welding Code, and the New York State Department of Transportation adds its own Steel Construction Manual on top for the steel it buys. Bridge fabrication brings the strictest controls a structural inspector meets: preheat on thicker plate, welder qualification checks, inspection of fracture-critical members and full traceability for every main member.

Across the river the rules change. Structural welding in Ontario follows Canadian standards, chiefly CSA W59, and Canadian fabricators are certified under CSA W47.1 through the Canadian Welding Bureau. The AWS CWI is an American credential; a Buffalo inspector asked to work on the Canadian side should check what that employer and that project require. Atlantis does not prepare candidates for CWB or CGSB certification.

Aerospace and precision manufacturing

Moog, which started in East Aurora in 1951 and is still headquartered in Western New York, employs more than 4,000 people in Erie County. In August 2026 it opened a 150,000-square-foot Advanced Integrated Manufacturing facility on its East Aurora campus for its military aircraft precision machining work, which produces tight-tolerance parts for flight control actuation systems. Moog's core work there is machining rather than welding, but the aerospace supply chain around it includes welded hardware, and aerospace welding is controlled by customer specifications, some of them built on AWS D17.1. An inspector in that world needs to read a customer specification as carefully as any code.

Joining research and metals

EWI, the Columbus-based joining and manufacturing technology organization, runs Buffalo Manufacturing Works at 683 Northland Avenue on the Northland campus in East Buffalo. It opened in 2015 on the Buffalo Niagara Medical Campus and moved to Northland in 2018. Its listed capabilities include arc welding and directed energy deposition, laser processes, resistance and solid-state welding, NDE and inspection, and structural integrity work, and its Shift 2.0 program supports small and medium-sized Western New York manufacturers. Metals production adds to the mix: the local AWS section has toured Aurubis Buffalo, a copper products plant, and Airgas's Buffalo operation, and has hosted events with the cutting equipment maker Koike in Arcade.

Plants, power and the rest of the industrial base

The region's engine and stamping plants, chemical works in Niagara Falls and hydroelectric stations on the Niagara River all keep maintenance welders busy. Power and process piping repairs follow ASME B31.1 and B31.3, with procedures and welders qualified under Section IX, and plant shutdowns create short periods of intense welding where an inspector's day is fit-up checks, welder qualification records and visual acceptance before NDT.

Who hires CWIs in Buffalo Niagara

  • Structural fabricators across New York State, including the shops that supplied the stadium, which keep CWIs on staff for shop quality control and customer audits.
  • Steel erectors and general contractors who need field weld inspection documented to D1.1.
  • Bridge fabricators and highway contractors working to D1.5 and NYSDOT requirements.
  • Testing and inspection firms that perform welding inspection for owners and building officials.
  • Manufacturers and aerospace suppliers that need someone to own weld quality and answer customer specifications.
  • Plant maintenance contractors serving power, chemical and metals plants, who want inspectors comfortable with Section IX and piping codes.

Hiring managers here ask the same three things: which code you know, whether your welding experience can be verified, and whether you can write a report that holds up when a customer or owner reviews it.

Which Part C code book fits Buffalo work?

Part C tests you open book on one code that you select. Choose the book you will actually use, because knowing it thoroughly matters more on the job than any one exam score.

Your Western New York workBook to considerReason
Stadium, building and industrial structural steel; shop fabricationAWS D1.1Governs welded steel structures other than bridges and pressure equipment
Highway bridges and NYSDOT steelAWS D1.5The bridge code, with fracture-critical rules; NYSDOT adds its own manual
Power, chemical and process plant pipingASME Section IX with B31.1 and B31.3Qualification plus power and process piping examination and acceptance
Aerospace hardware for customers that specify itAWS D17.1Fusion welding for aerospace applications
Steel gas lines and stationsAPI 1104Pipeline welding and acceptance
Aluminum structuresAWS D1.2Aluminum structural welding

The edition AWS examines is listed on your application and can be older than the newest edition in print, so study that one. See AWS D1.1, AWS D1.5 and the D1.1 acceptance criteria guide for background.

The AWS Niagara Frontier Section

The Buffalo area's AWS section is the Niagara Frontier Section, part of AWS District 6, with a site on sections.aws.org. Its recent program shows the range of the local industry: plant tours of Airgas Buffalo and Aurubis Buffalo, a weld-off competition, an evening on metal art with Koike in Arcade that drew 33 people in July 2026, and a volunteer day at Griffis Sculpture Park. For someone preparing for the CWI, section events are where you meet working inspectors and QC managers who can confirm your welding experience on the AWS application and tell you which local employers want certified inspectors. AWS membership also lowers AWS examination fees under the fee table AWS publishes on aws.org.

Where Western New York welders train

Erie 1 BOCES runs adult welding courses from West Seneca, and regional welding-school listings also include Niagara County Community College in Sanborn, Jamestown Community College and the SUNY College of Technology at Alfred. Ironworker, boilermaker and pipefitter apprenticeships train much of the structural and pipe welding workforce, and many plants train their own maintenance welders.

Schooling matters for the CWI because AWS trades education against experience. Completed trade or vocational courses leave four years of welding-related work to show; a high school diploma means five. Associate degrees in engineering technology, engineering or physical science bring it to two years, and a bachelor's in welding engineering or welding technology to one. AWS decides which row a given program fits, so check before relying on a shorter figure.

Booking the exam from Buffalo

When AWS approves your application, your confirmation letter includes an eligibility code. Use it to book Part A and Part C, both computer-based, at a Prometric test center; Prometric's site lists the centers nearest Buffalo. Part B is different: AWS runs the practical itself at its seminar and examination locations, so plan on travelling. Check the AWS seminar and exam schedule before anything else, choose a practical date you can reach, then fit the Prometric bookings into the order and window AWS gives you. In winter, leave slack for lake-effect snow when you plan the travel; a missed practical is an expensive way to lose a season.

Expect 150 questions on Part A, hands-on tasks with AWS-supplied tools and specimens plus 46 questions on Part B, and roughly 50 to 65 open-book questions on Part C. AWS requires 72 percent or more on every part. AWS publishes its examination fees on aws.org, and the CWI exam budget planner helps with the rest of the bill: travel, the code book and time off.

Study timing: construction season, winter and plant shutdowns

Western New York's calendar shapes when people can study. Outdoor structural and bridge work crowds into the warmer months, so ironworkers and field inspectors often have more time in winter. Plants schedule shutdowns when production allows. Shop fabricators follow their order books.

  • Field workers can use the winter months for the fundamentals and the code book, and keep the timed papers for the run-up to an early-season examination date.
  • Plant staff can work the online material around shift rotations, then use a one-to-one block to sharpen code navigation before an exam booked after a shutdown.
  • Everyone should practise practical measurement on real welds with real gauges, writing each reading down before comparing it with the acceptance criteria.

Corporate delivery at a Western New York fabricator or plant

The corporate format brings the full six days to one employer's site for a group of its staff. In Buffalo that could be a structural fabricator preparing more than one CWI for its quality plan, a bridge shop getting inspectors ready for D1.5 work, a manufacturer preparing QC leads ahead of customer audits, or a plant maintenance contractor building an in-house inspection team. The practical day uses the company's own fillet weld gauges, bridge cam gauges and undercut gauges on welds from its own floor, and the code day can split between books for a mixed group. Dates can be planned around the construction season or shutdowns. Each candidate still applies to AWS personally and must meet its eligibility and vision rules individually.

One-to-one sessions, online or in person

For a single candidate who wants direct coaching, the one-to-one format provides six days of sessions with the instructor, online or in person at a location agreed when booking. It suits an engineer who needs code-book speed more than theory, a QC lead whose company needs a CWI by a fixed date, or a candidate retaking one part who wants every session aimed at it. The outline does not change; the instructor adjusts the pace and emphasis to that one person.

Eligibility and the eye examination

Beyond the education and experience rules above, AWS requires a visual acuity record on its own form: near vision of Jaeger J2 at 12 inches or more, with or without corrective lenses, and a color perception test, carried out by an ophthalmologist, optometrist, physician, registered nurse or certified physician assistant, and recent enough under AWS rules on the day you sit the examination. Wearing reading glasses does not rule you out. If you are short of the CWI experience, the Certified Associate Welding Inspector (CAWI) has lower thresholds and lets you work alongside a CWI while you build your years. The full table is on the national CWI exam prep page, and CWI requirements and career impact covers the detail.

After the CWI: Buffalo career paths

AWS keeps the CWI valid for nine years, with renewal filings at the third and sixth years and recertification at the ninth. What comes next depends on where you work.

  • Senior CWI for those who end up running inspection programs; see the SCWI pathway.
  • Endorsements to add codes, useful for an inspector who moves between building steel and bridge work.
  • NDT methods for inspectors who want to test as well as look. Under ASNT SNT-TC-1A the employer certifies NDT personnel after training and documented method experience; Atlantis provides the training. See NDT training in Buffalo, VT Level 2, UT Level 2 and MT Level 2.

If you are weighing credentials, the AWS CWI vs API 577 vs ASNT Level II comparison lays them out; Atlantis does not train for API certifications. For inspection work in the area, see ultrasonic testing in Buffalo, magnetic particle testing in Buffalo, penetrant testing in Buffalo and inspection services in New York. The Practical NDT welding workshop runs in a browser for practice between study sessions.

Other northeastern CWI pages and a Buffalo quote

Related CWI exam prep pages: Cleveland, Pittsburgh, New York, Newark and Detroit. For difficulty by part, see CWI results by exam part.

For a quote, tell us which format you want, how many candidates, each person's schooling and welding history in outline, and the Part C book each plans to choose. For corporate delivery, add the facility location, the gauges and weld samples available, and the weeks that suit your season or shutdown plan. Request a Buffalo CWI exam prep quote; the price is quoted on request.

faq.q: Is there a CWI classroom in Buffalo?
faq.a: No. There is no Atlantis classroom in Buffalo. The six-day course is taken online at your own pace, as one-to-one sessions with the instructor (online or in person at a location agreed when booking), or as a corporate course at your employer's facility. See the outline.

AWS. The American Welding Society reviews applications, runs the three examination parts and issues the certification. Atlantis prepares candidates and certifies nobody, and AWS has not endorsed the course.

faq.q: Which Part C code suits structural work like the Highmark Stadium?
faq.a: AWS D1.1, the structural steel code for buildings and similar structures, which governs both shop and field welding on that kind of job. See AWS D1.1.

faq.q: I fabricate bridge steel for NYSDOT jobs. Which book should I choose?
faq.a: AWS D1.5, the Bridge Welding Code. NYSDOT adds its own Steel Construction Manual on top for the steel it buys, but D1.5 is the code book the examination offers for bridge work. See AWS D1.5.

faq.q: Does an AWS CWI let me inspect welding in Ontario?
faq.a: Not automatically. Structural welding in Canada follows CSA standards such as W59, and fabricators are certified under CSA W47.1 through the Canadian Welding Bureau. Check what the Canadian employer and project require. Atlantis does not prepare candidates for CWB or CGSB certification.

faq.q: Where do Buffalo candidates take the exam?
faq.a: Parts A and C are computer-based, booked at a Prometric center using the eligibility code from your AWS confirmation letter. Part B runs only at AWS seminar and examination locations, so expect to travel and allow for winter weather.

faq.q: Can the one-to-one sessions be held in person?
faq.a: Yes. One-to-one sessions run online or in person at a location agreed when you book, over six days, following the same outline as the other formats.

faq.q: Can a Western New York fabricator have the course run at its shop?
faq.a: Yes. The corporate format delivers the six days at your facility for a group of your staff, using your gauges, welds and, where it fits, your code. Each person applies to AWS individually. Ask for a quote.

faq.q: Do the practice questions come from AWS?
faq.a: No. They are original questions written by Atlantis to the topic areas AWS publishes. Atlantis does not see the live examination.

faq.q: Can I add NDT qualifications after the CWI?
faq.a: Yes. Atlantis provides ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based training in VT, MT, PT and UT; your employer certifies you under its written practice once training and experience are complete. See NDT training in Buffalo.
